# 📝 Notes

Jun 8, 2026

## Chameleon Profile Page Discussion

Invited [Austin Dillman](mailto:austin@chameleon.co) [Juan Morales](mailto:juan@chameleon.co) [Michael Saint-Aubin](mailto:michael.saint-aubin@chameleon.co) [Caleb Ludwick](mailto:caleb.ludwick@chameleon.co)

Attachments [Chameleon Profile Page Discussion](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/event?eid=NHR2cDJyZzdqZnVoMzFvMHJncWI3djQ1NXEgYXVzdGluQGNoYW1lbGVvbi5jbw)

Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SiZzaE36tbcjssPVZXT_NFdcI1AGuBkTfF1WUj5BGzk/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.oj23ukcqmes4) 

### Summary

Discussions regarding community profile redesigns focused on enhancing lead generation and enabling modular user customization options.

**Current Profile Inefficiencies**  
Static profiles fail to generate leads due to lack of visual appeal and relevant content. Contributors avoid utilizing them for pitches because the existing format is text-heavy and unpolished.

**Adopting Modular Design Approach**  
The team decided to implement a module-based builder that facilitates video integration, personalized testimonials, and flexible portfolio layouts. This approach prioritizes authenticity over standardized, long-form text blocks.

**Optimizing Inquiry Processes**  
New contact forms will include essential fields for budget and project timelines to improve lead quality. Contributors will retain control over vetting and managing direct inquiries from these profiles.

*Rate this Summary:* [Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4YkxrBAaiTVqYCi?isGoogler=false&isHelpful=true) or [Not Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4YkxrBAaiTVqYCi?isGoogler=false&isHelpful=false)

### Decisions

## ALIGNED

* **Implementation of client testimonial feature** The community profiles will include a feature for collecting and displaying client testimonials, similar to the functionality found on LinkedIn.

* **Lead ownership for profile-generated leads** Chameleons will receive full ownership and credit for leads generated directly through their individual community profile pages.

* **Administrative fee for profile leads** A 1-2% administrative fee will be applied to leads generated through the website to cover the collective's facilitation and management costs.

* **Project development process established** The project lifecycle is set for a six-week duration, consisting of feedback analysis, wireframe development, iterative stakeholder review, and a final handoff to the web implementation team.

We've **updated the Decisions section** using your feedback.

Let us know what you think: [Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5p6FWBVWvynleNU?isGoogler=no&isHelpful=yes) or [Not Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5p6FWBVWvynleNU?isGoogler=no&isHelpful=no)

### Next steps

- [ ] \[Austin Dillman, Juan Morales\] Research Video Profiles: Investigate if video profiles can be implemented as a new feature for the Chameleon profile pages to showcase authenticity and credibility.

- [ ] \[Austin Dillman, Juan Morales\] Build Profile Modules: Design and develop a modular system for individual Chameleon profile pages that allows users to toggle widgets like logo bars, testimonials, and portfolio work.

- [ ] \[Austin Dillman, Juan Morales\] Enable Testimonial Collection: Create a mechanism for Chameleons to request and collect client testimonials that will automatically populate on their personal Chameleon profile page.

- [ ] \[Austin Dillman, Juan Morales\] Define Referral Fee: Determine the fair referral fee structure for leads generated directly through individual Chameleon profile pages to incentivize user participation while covering site facilitation costs.

- [ ] \[Austin Dillman, Juan Morales\] Review Competitor Platforms: Analyze functionality of external freelance and contractor platforms. Use these insights to develop a frame of reference for the website redesign.

- [ ] \[Austin Dillman, Juan Morales\] Create Website Wireframes: Develop wireframes for the new version of the website based on feedback gathered during interviews. Share these designs with the participants to gather further insight.

### Details

*Did the screenshots in this section make your notes [better](https://goo.gle/44IH7J9) or [worse](https://goo.gle/4b5ZWtJ)?*

* **Meeting Purpose**: Juan Morales and Austin Dillman convened to gather input on the upcoming redesign of chameleon community profiles on the website. The goal is to ensure the new pages provide value to the community members and help facilitate work.

* **Current State of Profiles**: Caleb Ludwick noted that while they use the current profiles for pitches, the quality is inconsistent. Michael Saint-Aubin reported that they avoid using the website profiles entirely, favoring profile slides because they are easier to digest and provide more specific, relevant details ([00:04:10](#00:04:10)).

* **Emphasis on Relevancy**: Participants agreed that "thousand-skill" lists are ineffective. Michael Saint-Aubin and Caleb Ludwick emphasized that clients prioritize specific experience—such as industry background or expertise in a specific platform—over general descriptions when selecting a candidate ([00:05:37](#00:05:37)).

* **Effectiveness of Case Studies**: Michael Saint-Aubin observed that case studies are rarely reviewed by clients, estimating a 10% read rate, and are therefore not the primary driver for engagement ([00:08:52](#00:08:52)).

* **Incorporating Video**: Michael Saint-Aubin proposed integrating video profiles, such as short clips of previous collaborators or clients speaking about the chameleon's work, to build authenticity and credibility. Austin Dillman and Juan Morales agreed that this would effectively capture personality and humanize the profiles, which static text fails to do ([00:10:45](#00:10:45)).

* **Funnel Positioning**: Juan Morales suggested that profile pages are best suited for top-of-funnel discovery, while customized slides remain more effective for late-stage pitching where specific, tailored work examples are required ([00:13:22](#00:13:22)).

* **Profile Structure and Design**: Caleb Ludwick suggested the profiles should function more like personal homepages, incorporating a logo bar, case studies, and testimonials to better showcase an individual's unique background ([00:14:56](#00:14:56)).

* **User Customization**: Michael Saint-Aubin and Caleb Ludwick expressed strong interest in having control over their own pages, suggesting a widget or module-based builder that would allow them to curate their own content and select which elements (like testimonials or portfolios) to display ([00:15:45](#00:15:45)).

* **Contact Mechanisms**: Participants raised concerns about spam but preferred that inquiries sent via profiles go directly to them, potentially with pre-populated subject lines, rather than being handled through a generic mailbox ([00:17:43](#00:17:43)).

* **Testimonials**: Caleb Ludwick identified the lack of a dedicated space for testimonials as a major weakness in the current design and advocated for including a feature that allows clients to easily submit feedback to be displayed on the profile ([00:19:50](#00:19:50)).

* **Showcasing Work**: Michael Saint-Aubin and Caleb Ludwick stated that the current profiles do not adequately showcase work. They recommended a design that supports a more visual, portfolio-style layout rather than the current text-heavy format ([00:20:46](#00:20:46)) ([00:23:42](#00:23:42)).

* **Scalable Customization**: Austin Dillman explored the idea of using predefined modules—such as a portfolio module or a design module—to provide flexibility for customization while maintaining professional guardrails for the collective ([00:24:31](#00:24:31)).

* **Data and Lead Generation**: Juan Morales emphasized that the primary goal is lead generation. By connecting profiles more closely to actual project data and allowing users to customize their pages, the organization hopes to increase the number of leads that result from profile views ([00:26:21](#00:26:21)) ([00:28:10](#00:28:10)).

* **Referral Fee Structure**: The group discussed the fairness of referral fees for leads originating from the website. Austin Dillman and Michael Saint-Aubin suggested that if a lead is generated specifically through an individual's page, that person should receive the credit, with a nominal referral fee (approximately 1% to 2%) paid to the organization for administrative facilitation ([00:28:59](#00:28:59)) ([00:31:26](#00:31:26)).

* **Lead Vetting**: Austin Dillman and Caleb Ludwick discussed the level of support expected from the core team. Participants preferred that the core team filter out spam, but they expressed a desire to conduct their own due diligence on qualified leads rather than having the core team manage the entire vetting process ([00:34:16](#00:34:16)) ([00:37:58](#00:37:58)).

* **Referral Incentives**: Austin Dillman raised the question of whether chameleons would be incentivized to promote others on platforms like LinkedIn if there were a tracking mechanism for the referral. Michael Saint-Aubin noted that while promoting others is valuable, financial incentives might be complex unless they involve a warm introduction ([00:36:03](#00:36:03)).

* **Qualifying Inquiries**: To improve the quality of incoming leads, Caleb Ludwick and Michael Saint-Aubin suggested including fields in contact forms for budget, timeline, and internal resource requirements, noting that clients often have specific timelines even if they lack defined budgets ([00:38:47](#00:38:47)).

* **Value Articulation**: Michael Saint-Aubin suggested that profiles should do a better job of explaining the value proposition of hiring an individual chameleon versus an agency, specifically highlighting the lack of overhead and the direct access to experts ([00:42:04](#00:42:04)).

* **Process and "How I Work" Content**: Participants discussed the value of a "How I Work" module to explain their process. Caleb Ludwick and Michael Saint-Aubin were receptive to this, provided it did not pigeonhole them into specific offerings or force them to share confidential methods, but rather helped articulate their methodology ([00:44:24](#00:44:24)).

  ![][image1]

* **Personal Content**: Juan Morales asked about including non-work content. Caleb Ludwick and Michael Saint-Aubin felt this should be optional and could humanize the profile, provided it does not become a requirement ([00:49:21](#00:49:21)).

* **Competitive Benchmarking**: Austin Dillman noted that the team needs to research other hiring platforms to identify functional examples and best practices before finalizing the redesign ([00:52:51](#00:52:51)).

* **Peer Validation**: Juan Morales and Michael Saint-Aubin discussed implementing peer-to-peer video reviews as a low-hanging fruit to add authenticity, potentially serving as a better alternative to standard case studies ([00:54:50](#00:54:50)).

* **Collaboration Visibility**: Austin Dillman asked about showcasing frequent collaborators. Michael Saint-Aubin and Caleb Ludwick advised against explicitly listing "common collaborators" to avoid creating exclusive groups, preferring that peer validation be achieved through testimonials ([00:57:47](#00:57:47)).

* **Next Steps**: Juan Morales concluded by noting that the feedback-gathering process will continue for the next six weeks to ensure the website redesign meets the needs of the chameleons ([00:58:38](#00:58:38)).

* **Profile Page Usage and Design**: Juan Morales observed that usage of the profile pages is currently low, noting that they still have eight more people to interview to confirm these findings. While Caleb Ludwick actively uses the pages, others such as Michael Saint-Aubin were previously unaware of their existence, and Juan Morales emphasized the need to better capitalize on this resource. Regarding design, Caleb Ludwick noted that their own profile page is currently overcrowded, suggesting that the implementation of bite-sized content modules would significantly improve the layout and presentation ([00:59:29](#00:59:29)).

* **Project Roadmap and Collaboration**: Austin Dillman expressed appreciation for the participants' feedback, noting that they valued the insights provided despite the short notice. Juan Morales stated that the project will continue for six weeks, during which time the team will analyze the feedback and develop wireframes for the next iteration of the page. The team plans to keep the group involved by sharing these wireframes to solicit further insights while ensuring that they do not add an excessive workload to the participants. Finally, the team will hand off the completed designs to the website team for implementation ([01:00:18](#01:00:18)).
